title: Wrap Rate Policy Version Conflict Between Approved Gate Review and DCAA Audit Correction
scenario_text:
Context from Costpoint — Indirect Rate Module:
FY25 Provisional Rates (approved by DCAA): OH 58.2%, G&A 14.1%, Fringe 32.8%
FY26 Provisional Rates (submitted to DCAA, pending approval): OH 61.7%, G&A 13.9%, Fringe 33.1%
FY26 Bid Rates (used in active proposals per Feb 2026 gate review): OH 60.0%, G&A 14.0%, Fringe 33.0%

**SharePoint — /policies/finance/rate-application-guide.docx (v5.2, Mar 2025)**
Section 6.1: 'Active proposals shall use bid rates approved at the most recent Pricing Gate Review unless a DCAA determination modifies allowable cost composition, in which case the Financial Planning team will issue a Rate Advisory Memorandum (RAM) within 10 business days.'

**Email — Subject: 'DCAA Audit Finding - Material Handling Costs' (Mar 22, 2026)**
From: dcaa.auditor@dcaa.mil
To: d.kowalczyk@sentinel-ds.com (Controller)
CC: contracts-admin@sentinel-ds.com

'Per our review of incurred cost submission FY24, material handling costs currently included in your OH pool (approximately 3.2% of the pool) are more appropriately classified as a direct cost or separate indirect allocation per CAS 418. Please submit a revised rate structure within 30 days.'

**Teams — #finance-leadership (Mar 25, 2026, 10:02 AM)**
@d.kowalczyk: Heads up — DCAA finding on material handling. If we reclassify per CAS 418, OH drops ~3 points but we'd need a new material handling rate of about 4.8%.
@cfo.williams: Impact on active bids?
@d.kowalczyk: Depends on material content. High-material CLINs get more expensive, low-material CLINs get cheaper. Net impact varies by proposal.
@cfo.williams: Don't disrupt active proposals until we respond formally. Let's discuss Thursday.
@d.kowalczyk: Got it. No RAM until we have a final position.
[reacted with: thumbs-up emoji by @cfo.williams]

**Monday.com — VANGUARD Proposal (Army/INSCOM) | Due: Apr 25, 2026**
Pricing Status: Final — using Feb gate review rates
Material content: 38% of total CLIN value (highest in active portfolio)
Gold Team: Apr 15 (complete, no pricing findings)
Note from Gold Team lead: 'Pricing is tight. LPTA evaluation — we're within 2% of PTW target.'

**SharePoint — Gate Review Minutes (Feb 15, 2026):**
Attendees: CFO Williams, VP Capture, Controller Kowalczyk, Div. Presidents
Decision: 'FY26 bid rates approved as stated. Apply uniformly to all proposals in pipeline.'
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @m.santos, Feb 16]: 'What about the pending DCAA review of OH composition? Should we caveat these rates?' — Reply by @d.kowalczyk: 'Premature. Audit isn't complete. We'll adjust if needed.'

**Email — Subject: 'Rate question - VANGUARD' (Apr 12, 2026)**
From: w.tran@sentinel-ds.com
To: pricing-team@sentinel-ds.com

'VANGUARD is LPTA with heavy material. If DCAA forces the CAS 418 reclassification, our material handling adds ~4.8% to material costs. That's potentially $1.2M on our $25M material base. Are we still good with gate review rates or do we need to flag?'

[No response as of Apr 14]
question: For the VANGUARD proposal due April 25, should the pricing team continue using the February gate review rates or take action based on the DCAA finding?

contributor.name: William Tran
contributor.title: Solutions Architect & Proposal Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Government proposal pricing, LPTA vs best-value evaluation, teaming arrangements, technical volume writing

choices: Continue with February gate review rates as approved — the DCAA finding is not yet finalized and the CFO explicitly directed no disruption to active proposals.
Issue a RAM immediately and reprice VANGUARD using the projected post-reclassification rates (OH ~57%, MH 4.8%) since the CAS 418 finding creates a known cost risk.

Escalate to VP Capture for a risk-acceptance decision — the gate review rates are technically compliant but the unanswered pricing team email and high material content create a material (>$1M) cost risk on an LPTA bid that should be acknowledged before submission.
Delay VANGUARD submission and request an extension from the contracting officer until DCAA finalizes the rate determination.
